ei.title: Reading as a Loosely Related Set of Behaviors
ei.subject: 10월_2024 고2 모의고사
ei.lesson: Reading as a Loosely Related Set of Behaviors

fullPassage: Some people argue that there is a single, logically consistent concept known as reading that can be neatly set apart from everything else people do with books. Is reading really that simple? The most productive way to think about reading is as a loosely related set of behaviors that belong together owing to family resemblances, as Ludwig Wittgenstein used the phrase, without having in common a single defining trait. Consequently, efforts to distinguish reading from nonreading are destined to fail because there is no agreement on what qualifies as reading in the first place. The more one tries to figure out where the border lies between reading and not-reading, the more edge cases will be found to stretch the term's flexible boundaries. Thus, it is worth attempting to collect together these exceptional forms of reading into a single forum, one highlighting the challenges faced by anyone wishing to establish the boundaries where reading begins and ends. The attempt moves toward an understanding of reading as a spectrum that is expansive enough to accommodate the distinct reading activities.

questions.passage: Some people argue that there is a single, logically (A)[consistent / contradictory] concept known as reading that can be neatly set apart from everything else people do with books. Is reading really that simple? The most productive way to think about reading is as a loosely related set of behaviors that (B)[belong / differ] together owing to family resemblances, as Ludwig Wittgenstein used the phrase, without having in common a single defining trait. Consequently, efforts to distinguish reading from nonreading are destined to fail because there is no agreement on what qualifies as reading in the first place. The more one tries to figure out where the border lies between reading and not-reading, the more edge cases will be found to stretch the term's (C)[flexible / rigid] boundaries. Thus, it is worth attempting to collect together these exceptional forms of reading into a single forum, one highlighting the challenges faced by anyone wishing to establish the boundaries where reading begins and ends. The attempt moves toward an understanding of reading as a spectrum that is expansive enough to accommodate the distinct reading activities.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: (A) 논리적으로 일관된(consistent) 개념. (B) 함께 속하는(belong) 행동들. (C) 유연한(flexible) 경계.
det.analysis:
✅ ② consistent – belong – flexible: 모두 원문 적합 ←정답
❌ ① contradictory(모순되는)는 '논리적으로 일관된'이라는 흐름과 반대
❌ ③ differ(다르다)는 행동들이 '함께 속한다(belong)'는 문맥과 반대
❌ ④ rigid(경직된)는 경계가 '유연하다(flexible)'는 문맥과 반대
det.tip: consistent(일관된) ↔ contradictory(모순된) / belong(속하다) ↔ differ(다르다) / flexible(유연한) ↔ rigid(경직된)

questions.passage: Some people argue that there is a single, logically consistent concept known as reading that can be neatly set apart from everything else people do with books. Is reading really that simple? Consequently, efforts to (B)[distinguish / combine] reading from nonreading are destined to fail because there is no agreement on what qualifies as reading in the first place. The more one tries to figure out where the border lies between reading and not-reading, the more edge cases will be found to stretch the term's flexible boundaries. Thus, it is worth attempting to collect together these exceptional forms of reading into a single forum, one highlighting the challenges faced by anyone wishing to establish the boundaries where reading begins and ends. The attempt moves toward an understanding of reading as a spectrum that is (C)[expansive / narrow] enough to accommodate the distinct reading activities.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: (A) 가장 생산적인(productive) 방법. (B) 읽기와 비읽기를 구별하려는(distinguish) 노력. (C) 충분히 광범위한(expansive) 스펙트럼.
det.analysis:
✅ ④ productive – distinguish – expansive: 모두 원문 적합 ←정답
❌ ① useless(쓸모없는)는 '가장 생산적인(productive)' 방법과 반대
❌ ② combine(결합하다)은 둘을 '구별하려(distinguish)' 한다는 문맥과 반대
❌ ③ narrow(좁은)는 스펙트럼이 '광범위하다(expansive)'는 문맥과 반대
det.tip: productive(생산적인) ↔ useless(쓸모없는) / distinguish(구별하다) ↔ combine(결합하다) / expansive(광범위한) ↔ narrow(좁은)

questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: (A) 깔끔하게(neatly) 구분되다. (B) 예외적인(exceptional) 형태의 읽기. (C) 서로 다른(distinct) 읽기 활동.

❌ ② carelessly(부주의하게)는 '깔끔하게(neatly)' 구분된다는 문맥과 반대

det.tip: neatly(깔끔하게) ↔ carelessly(부주의하게) / exceptional(예외적인) ↔ ordinary(평범한) / distinct(뚜렷이 다른) ↔ identical(동일한)

questions.passage:
(A) She carefully <u>set</u> her cup down on the wooden table before she began to speak.

(B) The teacher handed each student a <u>set</u> of colored pencils for the drawing class.
questions.stem: 다음 (A)와 (B)의 밑줄 친 set의 문맥적 의미로 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: (A) set ~ down = (물건을) 놓다. (B) a set of pencils = 한 세트/한 벌.
det.analysis:
✅ ③ (A) 놓다 – (B) 한 세트 ←정답
❌ ① (A) (액체가) 굳다는 컵을 내려놓는 문맥과 부적합
❌ ② (B) 정하다는 색연필 한 벌 문맥과 부적합
❌ ④ (A) 정하다는 컵을 내려놓는 문맥과 부적합
det.tip: set: (물건을) 놓다 / 한 세트·한 벌 / (액체가) 굳다.

det.korean: 둘 이상의 대상이 서로 비슷한 점.
det.analysis:
✅ ④ resemblance(유사성, 닮음): 서로 비슷한 점을 뜻함 ←정답
❌ ① difference(차이) 반대
❌ ② argument(논쟁) 부적합
❌ ③ distance(거리) 부적합

questions.passage: Thus, it is worth attempting to collect together these exceptional forms of reading into a single forum, one highlighting the challenges __________ (face) by anyone wishing to establish the boundaries where reading begins and ends. The attempt moves toward an understanding of reading as a spectrum that is expansive enough to accommodate the distinct reading activities.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 문맥에 맞게 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 (1단어) (영어로) 쓰시오.

det.korean: the challenges __________ (face) by anyone → 명사 뒤 수동 수식(과거분사) → faced.
det.analysis:
빈칸은 명사 'challenges(도전)' 바로 뒤에서 그 명사를 꾸며 주는 자리예요. '누군가에 의해 마주하게 되는' 도전이라는 수동의 뜻이라, 동사에 -ed를 붙인 과거분사를 써요. 원형 face → 과거분사 faced.
the challenges faced by anyone = 누군가가 마주하는 도전들.
det.tip: 명사 + 과거분사(수동 수식) → challenges faced by ~.

questions.passage: Consequently, efforts to distinguish reading from nonreading are __________ (destine) to fail because there is no agreement on what qualifies as reading in the first place. The more one tries to figure out where the border lies between reading and not-reading, the more edge cases will be found.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 문맥에 맞게 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 (1단어) (영어로) 쓰시오.

det.korean: efforts ~ are __________ (destine) to fail → be동사 뒤 수동(과거분사) → destined.
det.analysis:
빈칸은 'are ____ to fail'로 be동사(are) 뒤 자리예요. '실패하도록 정해져 있다'라는 수동의 뜻을 나타내려면 과거분사를 써요. 원형 destine → 과거분사 destined.
be destined to + 동사원형 = ~할 운명이다.
det.tip: be destined to ~(~할 운명이다). destine → destined.

questions.passage: Some people argue that there is a single, logically consistent concept known as reading that can be neatly set apart from everything else people do with books. Is reading really that simple? The most productive way to think about reading is as a loosely related set of behaviors that belong together owing to family resemblances, as Ludwig Wittgenstein used the phrase, without having in common a single defining trait. Consequently, efforts to distinguish reading from nonreading are destined to fail because there is no agreement on what qualifies as reading __________. The more one tries to figure out where the border lies between reading and not-reading, the more edge cases will be found to stretch the term's flexible boundaries. Thus, it is worth attempting to collect together these exceptional forms of reading into a single forum, one highlighting the challenges faced by anyone wishing to establish the boundaries where reading begins and ends. The attempt moves toward an understanding of reading as a spectrum that is expansive enough to accommodate the distinct reading activities.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 애초에(in the first place) 무엇이 읽기로 인정되는지에 대한 합의가 없다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① in the first place(애초에): no agreement on what qualifies as reading ____(애초에 무엇이 읽기인지 합의가 없다)로 자연스러움 ←정답
❌ ② at any cost(어떤 대가를 치르더라도) 문맥 부적합
❌ ③ for a long time(오랫동안) 부적합
❌ ④ by the way(그런데) 부적합

questions.passage: Some people argue that there is a single, logically consistent concept known as reading that can be neatly __________ everything else people do with books. Is reading really that simple? The most productive way to think about reading is as a loosely related set of behaviors that belong together owing to family resemblances, as Ludwig Wittgenstein used the phrase, without having in common a single defining trait. Consequently, efforts to distinguish reading from nonreading are destined to fail because there is no agreement on what qualifies as reading in the first place. The more one tries to figure out where the border lies between reading and not-reading, the more edge cases will be found to stretch the term's flexible boundaries. Thus, it is worth attempting to collect together these exceptional forms of reading into a single forum, one highlighting the challenges faced by anyone wishing to establish the boundaries where reading begins and ends. The attempt moves toward an understanding of reading as a spectrum that is expansive enough to accommodate the distinct reading activities.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 읽기라는 개념이 사람들이 책으로 하는 다른 모든 것과 깔끔하게 구분될(set apart from) 수 있다.
det.analysis:
✅ ③ set apart from(~와 구분되다): a concept ~ that can be neatly ____ everything else(다른 모든 것과 깔끔하게 구분되는 개념)로 자연스러움 ←정답
❌ ① mixed up with(~와 뒤섞이다) 문맥 반대
❌ ② combined with(~와 결합되다) 반대
❌ ④ hidden behind(~뒤에 숨겨지다) 부적합
